gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-sundane: Grandstander draws bold, expressive letters with strokes of constant width and short ascenders. And Noto Sans Sundanese stays quieter, with open-mouthed e crossbars and a lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar:
Grandstander gives round bowls whose walls never swell or thin.

Noto Sans Sunuwar follows with curves that leave daylight, like a rope's open bight, so a long passage should read approachably and without strain.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-syloti-: Every outline in Grandstander keeps one steady thickness, bold and expressive with short ascenders. And Noto Sans Syloti Nagri carries a long passage in a plain sans, its a opening to breathe at the lower bowl.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-syriac-: Grandstander cuts every stroke to a single width, giving its bold, expressive letters a short-ascender, tall-lowercase look. Noto Sans Syriac Western holds its terminals far from the stroke.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Grandstander has no stress in any curve, so its bold letters look drawn with one tool. But Noto Sans Tagalog, a sans with a dominant middle zone, probably wants a modest size to let its generous gaps work.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-tagbanw: Bowls with no thinning at the sides give Grandstander a bold, expressive roundness, with short ascenders and a tall lowercase. It earns its keep large and brief; Noto Sans Tagbanwa goes plain.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Grandstander has a smooth, drawn-wire feel across a whole sentence, bold and expressive. But Noto Sans Tai Le tapers its ink strokes before they touch, and a long stretch keeps an approachable, minimal step from capitals to lowercase.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-tai-tha: Chunky, bold wire-like lettering with horizontals as thick as the verticals, and short ascenders on a tall lowercase. Noto Sans Tai Tham crowds its chalk-board lowercase beneath it, keeping each c clearly visible.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-tai-vie: Grandstander looks like bent wire sign lettering, bold and constant in thickness, while Noto Sans Tai Viet reads in a plain sans. And the heading font does its best work as expressive display, where the body font keeps terminals pulled back from each curve.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-noto-sans-takri: Noto Sans Takri reads with a generously unclosed curve on every small round letter and a high-waisted lowercase. Grandstander does bold, expressive display, drawn on a single track width like neon tubing, while Noto Sans Takri does the quieter sans-serif work.
